formal_record.question:
The arrangement shown consists of square tiles of different sizes. The smallest tile has a perimeter of $80 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the length of the path shown along the edges of the tiles?
Choices:
A:$380 \mathrm{~cm}$
B:$400 \mathrm{~cm}$
C:$420 \mathrm{~cm}$
D:$440 \mathrm{~cm}$
E:$1680 \mathrm{~cm}$

mechanism: A complete smallest-square perimeter is paired by red with one unit of the indicated path. The given80cm is the perimeter, so this pair targets misbinding the80cm whole-perimeter measure as the path-unit length, producing21*80=1680cm (E) instead of dividing by4.
mathematical_solution: The smallest tile perimeter80 gives side20cm. In smallestsideunits the eleven pathsegments have lengths1,1,2,2,2,2,2,3,4,1,1 summing21. Hence length420cm, optionC unique. A perimeter80 must not be substituted for one side. Originalhead, eye, topology and all tile boundaries remain unchanged.
marker_roles: tile6 redoutline marks exactly the entire perimeter of a smallesttile, the geometric quantity whose80cm is stated.
thick_snake0 red marks a single smallestside length along the actual path, the location where the whole-perimeter quantity could be wrongly substituted.
The two overlays together carry a perimeter-to-pathunit binding; no option or irrelevanttile is colored.
human_gate: The connected snake/path and head remain readily identifiable even with one short segment colored. No new path, lengthlabel, equality or other mathematicalcondition is added.
